issue.title: Athena daily, weekly, and monthly backup rotations are stale; confirm they advance after the rsync-24 fix

task_type_fields.impact:
The daily, weekly, and monthly recovery points are 6 days, 4 weeks, and 6 months old. If
these tiers fail for a reason other than exit 24, hourly rotations are the only fresh
backups. Hourly retention is short, so older content loss would go unrecoverable.
task_type_fields.repro:
`verify_root_cron.py` (tailnet `hosts/athena/root-cron/`, run as bryan on athena,
2026-10-23 16:43 EDT) reports the hourly marker fresh (835 s), but:

```
live daily rotation: root-owned, marker 5.7d old   (last 2026-10-18)
live weekly rotation: root-owned, marker 27.6d old (last 2026-09-26)
live monthly rotation: root-owned, marker 183.6d old (last 2026-04-23)
```

Epic bob-cli-an.6 (phase 6.2, tailnet `0d0e2dd`) made `/usr/local/lib/athena-cron/backup.sh`
commit a rotation when rsync's only failure is exit 24 (vanished files). It proved two
consecutive scheduled **hourly** commits. Every tier sources that same file, but the
daily, weekly, and monthly tiers have not run since the install (2026-10-23 15:06 EDT):

- anacron spool mtimes: `cron.daily` 2026-10-23 00:54, `cron.weekly` 2026-10-17 01:38,
  `cron.monthly` 2026-10-21 01:47. Daily and weekly are due on the first anacron pass
  of 2026-10-24 (about 00:30-01:30 EDT); monthly is due about 2026-11-21.
- The failure cause of those tiers was never observed. Root mail had 0 daily/weekly/monthly
  messages because `/etc/anacrontab` sets `MAILTO=bryanbugyi34@gmail.com`, so their output
  goes to Gmail. The lander could not read it because the `gog` OAuth token had expired.
- The tiers also back up `/bin /boot /etc /lib32 /lib64 /opt /sbin /usr /var`, and rsync
  exit 23 (partial transfer) stays fatal by design. 40 hourly messages showed code 23.

Check: after 2026-10-24 02:00 EDT run
`python3 -I hosts/athena/root-cron/verify_root_cron.py` as bryan. The daily and weekly
markers must be under a day old, and `home/daily` and `home/daily-2` must differ. If a tier
is still stale, read the anacron mail (Gmail, after `gog auth` is restored by Bryan) or
use a reviewed `/sase_sudo` read of the job output to find the failing code. Do not run a
live backup by hand to test it. Recheck monthly after 2026-11-21.

issue.creation_reason: Proposed by phase bob-cli-an.6.2 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #3): the rsync-24 commit fix was proven only on hourly runs, and the daily/weekly/monthly tiers' own failure cause was never observed before the epic landed.

payload.description: 1a's rsync-24 fix was proven on hourly only; this confirms the other tiers

payload.entry: Verified by lander bob-cli-an.6.6 on 2026-10-24 ~04:05 EDT: tailnet verify_root_cron.py as bryan passed 105/105. The first scheduled anacron pass after the rsync-24 fix advanced both stale tiers. home/daily marker 1792816971 (2026-10-24 00:42 EDT, ~3h) is newer than daily-2 1792298910 (the old 2026-10-18 daily, preserved). home/weekly marker 1792819164 (2026-10-24 01:19 EDT) is newer than weekly-2 1790399942 (the old 2026-09-26 weekly). Hourly is fresh. Phase bob-cli-an.6.6.2 restore samples daily/bryan/.bashrc and weekly/bryan/.bashrc are md5-identical to live ~/.bashrc, and rotation contents differ. No live backup was run by hand. Monthly (marker 2026-04-23) is accepted on the shared backup.sh commit path (exit 0 or 24 commits, 23 stays fatal), which all three tiers source, plus the phase's scratch monthly-shaped rotation and TOO_SOON exercise. Its next scheduled run is the @monthly anacron pass around 2026-11-21. No tier-specific change was needed.
